2303	### Main-thread timing from a real hang (macapp) — WORKROOM-2B follow-up
2304	
2305	**What:** a bounded way to learn *how long* the main thread was held, and by what, from a hang report on
2306	a user's machine. Three candidates: Sentry profiling started and stopped around suspect windows,
2307	`os_signpost` intervals around panel body passes, or a watchdog breadcrumb capturing what the app was
2308	doing when the stall began.
2309	
2310	**Why:** WORKROOM-2B cost a full session of inference because the report was a single unsymbolicated
2311	main-thread sample. The dSYM upload fix (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml` + `Scripts/release.sh`) closes
2312	the *naming* half — frames will have function names now. Nothing tells us the duration or the shape of
2313	the stall.
2314	
2315	**Verify FIRST, before implementing anything:** whether Sentry's continuous profile chunks actually
2316	attach to macOS **app-hang** events. If they don't, profiling buys nothing for this use case and the
2317	signpost/breadcrumb options win. `Core/SentryConfig.swift` already configures profiling with
2318	`.trace` lifecycle and `sessionSampleRate = 1.0`, but the app opens no transactions, so it never runs —
2319	that is why the option looked free and isn't.
2320	
2321	**Known caveat (from the eng review):** sentry-cocoa 9.19's manual lifecycle requires an explicit
2322	`SentrySDK.stopProfiler()`. A launch-start-never-stop profiler is outside documented usage, costs CPU
2323	and upload volume continuously, and could itself stall — which is why it was cut from the fix rather
2324	than shipped on nightly.

59	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

61	      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

63	      # protoc is a build-time dep of jj-lib. The `jj` CLI is what the working_status fixtures shell
64	      # out to for repo setup (and the test SKIPS silently without it, so it must be installed) —
65	      # apt has no jj package, hence the release tarball. $JJ_VERSION comes from the
66	      # workflow-level env: above.
67	      - name: Install protoc + jj
68	        run: |
69	          sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq protobuf-compiler
70	          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/releases/download/v$JJ_VERSION/jj-v$JJ_VERSION-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz" \
71	            | sudo tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin ./jj

73	
74	      # Pinned for the lint gates below, unlike the `app` job (which deliberately tracks the runner's
75	      # rustc so a toolchain bump invalidates its output cache). rustfmt's layout and clippy's lint set
76	      # both change between releases, so an unpinned toolchain makes `--check` and `-D warnings` fail
77	      # when GitHub rolls its image rather than when someone's code is wrong. Same reasoning as the
78	      # pinned golangci-lint in `cli`. Keep in step with the local toolchain.
79	      - name: Install Rust 1.96.1
80	        run: |
81	          rustup toolchain install 1.96.1 --profile minimal --component rustfmt,clippy
82	          rustup default 1.96.1

84	      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
85	        with:
86	          workspaces: vcs
87	
88	      # Ordered cheapest-first so a formatting nit doesn't wait on the jj-lib crate graph.
89	      - name: Format
90	        run: cargo fmt --manifest-path vcs/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
91	
92	      - name: Clippy
93	        run: cargo clippy --manifest-path vcs/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
94	
95	      - name: Test
96	        run: cargo test --manifest-path vcs/Cargo.toml

98	  app:
99	    runs-on: macos-15
100	    steps:
101	      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
102	
103	      # Xcode 16+ bundles swift-format (used by `make app-lint`) and builds for macOS 14+.
104	      - uses: maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode@v1
105	        with:
106	          xcode-version: latest-stable
107	
108	      # Scripts/build-helper.sh compiles + embeds the workroom CLI during the test build.
109	      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
110	        with:
111	          go-version-file: go.mod
112	
113	      # XcodeGen generates the (gitignored) .xcodeproj. protobuf provides protoc, a build-time
114	      # dependency of jj-lib (the Rust VCS core, built by `make app-vcs`). aws/tap ships
115	      # pre-tapped but untrusted on the runner image, which makes every `brew install` on this
116	      # job emit a "tap trust" warning annotation unrelated to our formulae.
117	      - name: Install XcodeGen + protobuf
118	        run: |
119	          brew untap aws/tap
120	          brew install xcodegen protobuf
121	
122	      # jj (Jujutsu) is required by WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests, which exercise the VCS status
123	      # resolver against real git + jj repos. git + gh are preinstalled on the runner; jj is not.
124	      # Installed from the pinned release tarball (same mechanism as the `cli`/`vcs-core` jobs
125	      # above) rather than `brew install jj`, so this job tracks the same $JJ_VERSION instead of
126	      # whatever Homebrew resolves that day. macos-15 runners are Apple Silicon (arm64).
127	      - name: Install jj
128	        run: |
129	          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/releases/download/v$JJ_VERSION/jj-v$JJ_VERSION-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz" \
130	            | sudo tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin ./jj
131	          jj --version
132	
133	      - name: Lint (swift-format --strict)
134	        run: make app-lint
135	
136	      # The Rust VCS core (jj-lib via UniFFI) the app links. `make app-vcs` runs
137	      # vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh to produce the WrVcs package's xcframework + Swift bindings, and
138	      # MUST run before SPM resolves that local package below. Rust is preinstalled on the runner.
139	      #
140	      # Cache the *outputs*, not cargo's state: they only change when vcs/ (or the compiler) does,
141	      # which most commits don't touch, so the whole ~4min crate-graph build is skipped outright.
142	      # The key mirrors the input hash build-apple.sh stamps, so a restored set is also a no-op for
143	      # the app-vcs dep of `make app-test` below. rustc's version is in the key because it's in that
144	      # hash — leaving it out would mean a toolchain bump hits the cache, rebuilds anyway, and (the
145	      # primary key having hit) never saves the result.
146	      - name: Rust toolchain version (cache key input)
147	        id: rust
148	        run: |
149	          # e.g. "rustc 1.96.1 (31fca3adb 2026-06-26)" → "1.96.1-31fca3adb" (cache-key-safe).
150	          echo "version=$(rustc --version | awk '{print $2 "-" $3}' | tr -d '()')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
151	
152	      - name: Cache VCS core outputs
153	        id: vcs-core
154	        uses: actions/cache@v4
155	        with:
156	          path: |
157	            vcs/swift/WrVcs/Frameworks
158	            vcs/swift/WrVcs/Sources/WrVcs/wr_vcs_uniffi.swift
159	            vcs/swift/WrVcs/Sources/wr_vcs_uniffiFFI/include
160	          key: >-
161	            wrvcs-${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}-${{
162	            hashFiles('vcs/**/*.rs', 'vcs/**/Cargo.toml', 'vcs/Cargo.lock', 'vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh') }}
163	
164	      # Cold path only (vcs/ changed): keep cargo itself incremental. Swatinem/rust-cache rather than
165	      # a hand-rolled actions/cache of ~/.cargo + vcs/target, which restored a target/ whose
166	      # fingerprints were always stale — every run recompiled all 257 crates on a cache *hit*, and
167	      # the hit meant the useless cache was never re-saved.
168	      - name: Cache cargo (cold path)
169	        if: steps.vcs-core.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
170	        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
171	        with:
172	          workspaces: vcs
173	
174	      - name: Build VCS core (Rust → xcframework + Swift bindings)
175	        if: steps.vcs-core.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
176	        run: make app-vcs
177	
178	      # SPM resolves ~15 packages (Sparkle, Sentry, libghostty, the tree-sitter grammars, and
179	      # swift-syntax pulled transitively) by cloning them from GitHub on every run. Cache the
180	      # resolved checkouts keyed on project.yml (the sole source of the dependency set — the
181	      # .xcodeproj is xcodegen-generated and gitignored) so an unchanged set skips the network
182	      # entirely. The restore-keys fallback reuses an older cache after a dep change so only the
183	      # delta is fetched.
184	      - name: Cache SPM packages
185	        id: spm
186	        uses: actions/cache@v4
187	        with:
188	          path: macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages
189	          key: spm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('macapp/project.yml') }}
190	          restore-keys: spm-${{ runner.os }}-
191	
192	      # Compiling the dependency graph — libgit2 (429 tasks), SwiftGitX, the tree-sitter grammars,
193	      # Sentry, Sparkle, swift-syntax — is ~60% of the build's work and none of it changes between
194	      # runs. Caching the build dir lets xcodebuild's incremental check reuse those objects; only our
195	      # own sources rebuild (checkout gives them fresh mtimes, while the restored dep checkouts keep
196	      # their original ones, so the dependency objects stay up to date).
197	      #
198	      # Deliberately NO run-id suffix or restore-keys: the key is exactly what the dep objects depend
199	      # on (compiler + the dependency set), so the first run saves and every later run hits without
200	      # paying to re-upload ~500MB each time. actions/cache is post-if success(), so a failed build's
201	      # dir is never saved.
202	      - name: Xcode version (cache key input)
203	        id: xcode
204	        run: |
205	          # e.g. "Xcode 26.0" + "Build version 17A324" → "26.0-17A324".
206	          echo "version=$(xcodebuild -version | awk 'NR==1{v=$2} NR==2{b=$NF} END{print v "-" b}')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
207	
208	      - name: Cache Xcode build dir
209	        uses: actions/cache@v4
210	        with:
211	          path: macapp/DerivedData/Build
212	          key: >-
213	            xcbuild-${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.xcode.outputs.version }}-${{
214	            hashFiles('macapp/project.yml') }}
215	
216	      # Resolve up front with retries so a transient github.com blip mid-clone can't fail the whole
217	      # run (it did: swift-syntax clone hit "Couldn't connect to server"). The subsequent app-test
218	      # build reuses these checkouts via the same -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath, so it won't re-clone.
219	      #
220	      # Skipped on an exact cache hit: there's nothing to clone, so the whole step (~25s, including an
221	      # xcodegen run that `make app-test` does again anyway) is pure overhead. A restore-keys-only
222	      # (partial) restore reports no cache-hit, so a dependency change still resolves here, retries
223	      # and all.
224	      - name: Resolve SPM packages (retry on network flake)
225	        if: steps.spm.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
226	        working-directory: macapp
227	        run: |
228	          xcodegen generate
229	          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
230	            xcodebuild -project WorkroomApp.xcodeproj -scheme WorkroomApp \
231	              -derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages \
232	              -resolvePackageDependencies && exit 0
233	            echo "::warning::SPM resolve attempt $attempt failed; retrying in 15s"
234	            sleep 15
235	          done
236	          echo "::error::SPM resolve failed after 3 attempts"; exit 1
237	
238	      # Hosted runners have no signing cert / dev team: ad-hoc sign, clear the team, manual
239	      # style so xcodebuild won't provision against Apple's servers. Lets the non-sandboxed
240	      # app build and the unit tests launch their host app. (`make app-test` also builds.)
241	      - name: Test
242	        run: >-
243	          make app-test
244	          APP_SIGN_FLAGS="CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=YES DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="
245	
246	      # The supervisor PTY integration test (issue #7) drives the real supervisor.sh under a pty with
247	      # a fake server — the only gate on the no-orphan / no-"already running" behaviour the Swift unit
248	      # tests (mocked seam) can't see. python3 is preinstalled on the macOS runner.
249	      - name: Test (run-command supervisor)
250	        run: make app-test-supervisor
251	
252	      # Shell-script tests. `make app-test` builds Debug with a single native arch, so it can never
253	      # exercise build-helper.sh's multi-arch path — the branch whose absence shipped an arm64-only
254	      # CLI inside every universal .app. These run it directly with ARCHS="arm64 x86_64".
255	      - name: Test (build + channel helper scripts)
256	        run: make app-test-scripts

5	# per-day tags accumulate. The release TITLE holds the resolved version ("<base>-nightly.<count>")
6	# and doubles as the "already built this commit" marker for the skip guard — it is written only

25	  # incpatch(latest reachable tag) — a prerelease tag targets its own release (v2.0.0-beta.21 →
26	  # 2.0.0), a stable tag bumps patch (v1.3.0 → 1.3.1). The commit count is the monotonic ordering
27	  # key the CLI + Sparkle compare on.

jobs:
  cli:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Matrix over jj CLI versions the Go tests shell out to (see the "Install jj" step below) —
    # NOT the same axis as $JJ_VERSION above, which stays the single version `app`'s fixed-cost
    # macOS job installs. This caught a real bug (2026-08-16): fixtures shelling to `jj` assumed
    # 0.44's "auto-advance @ off an immutable tip after push" and silently broke on 0.43, where
    # `jj` behaves differently. Keep this list and vcs-core's in sync — both exercise the same
    # CLI-shelling concern from different languages. Bump when jj cuts a new release worth
    # covering; no need to chase every patch release.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        jj-version: ["0.43.0", "0.44.0"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

      # out to — both `t.Skip` silently without it, so without this step they never ran in CI at
      # all. Same pattern as the `vcs-core` job below (apt has no jj package, hence the release
      # tarball).
      - name: Install jj
        env:
          JJ_VERSION: ${{ matrix.jj-version }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/releases/download/v$JJ_VERSION/jj-v$JJ_VERSION-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz" \

257	  static func bundledBinaryURL() throws -> URL {

259	      return url
260	    }
261	    let exeDir = Bundle.main.bundleURL.deletingLastPathComponent()
262	    let candidate = exeDir.appendingPathComponent("workroom")
263	    if FileManager.default.isExecutableFile(atPath: candidate.path) {
264	      return candidate

266	    throw WorkroomCLIError.binaryMissing

271	  private func decode<T: Decodable>(_ type: T.Type, from result: CLIResult) throws -> T {
272	    try throwIfError(result)
273	    do {
274	      return try JSONDecoder().decode(type, from: result.stdout)
275	    } catch {
276	      throw WorkroomCLIError.decodeFailed(raw: String(data: result.stdout, encoding: .utf8) ?? "")
277	    }
278	  }

280	  /// Inspects the result and throws if it represents a failure. The CLI writes one
281	  /// JSON envelope to stdout for both success and error; a non-zero exit means error.
282	  private func throwIfError(_ result: CLIResult) throws {
283	    // A child killed by a signal — our timeout's `terminate()` (SIGTERM), or a SIGTERM the
284	    // system delivers around sleep/wake — reports the *signal number* as `terminationStatus`,
285	    // not a CLI exit code. Surfacing that as "workroom exited with code 15" was wrong (15 ==
286	    // SIGTERM); treat it as a timeout so it isn't mistaken for a real CLI failure.
287	    if result.timedOut || result.signaled { throw WorkroomCLIError.timedOut }
288	    if result.exitCode == 0 { return }
289	    if let env = try? JSONDecoder().decode(Envelope.self, from: result.stdout),
290	      let body = env.error
291	    {
292	      throw WorkroomCLIError.cli(kind: body.kind, message: body.message)
293	    }
294	    throw WorkroomCLIError.nonzero(code: result.exitCode, stderr: result.stderr)
295	  }
296	
297	  // MARK: Process execution
298	
299	  /// Runs the helper with `args`, draining stdout (read to end for the single JSON
300	  /// envelope) and stderr (read incrementally so `onLog` fires per NDJSON line as the
301	  /// script runs) concurrently, and enforcing a timeout. On timeout the process is
302	  /// terminated then killed.
303	  ///
304	  /// `userInitiated` selects the environment the child gets. The commands that run the user's own
305	  /// setup/teardown scripts get the full probed environment, so those scripts see the shell they
306	  /// were written against. Everything else (`list`, `add-project`) takes PATH only — a cheap,
307	  /// frequent read has no reason to carry the user's whole environment.
308	  private func run(
309	    _ args: [String], timeout: TimeInterval, userInitiated: Bool = false,
310	    onEvent: ((StreamEvent) -> Void)? = nil
311	  ) async throws -> CLIResult {
312	    let url = try Self.bundledBinaryURL()
313	    return try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
314	      let proc = Process()
315	      proc.executableURL = url
316	      proc.arguments = args
317	
318	      var env: [String: String]
319	      if userInitiated {
320	        env = ShellEnvironment.environment()
321	      } else {
322	        env = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
323	        env["PATH"] = ShellEnvironment.path()
324	      }
325	      env["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT"] = "0"
326	      env["GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS"] = "0"
327	      proc.environment = env
328	
329	      let outPipe = Pipe()
330	      let errPipe = Pipe()
331	      proc.standardOutput = outPipe
332	      proc.standardError = errPipe
333	
334	      let state = RunState()
335	      let collector = StderrCollector(onEvent: onEvent)
336	      let drain = DispatchGroup()
337	
338	      drain.enter()
339	      DispatchQueue.global().async {
340	        state.setStdout(outPipe.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile())
341	        drain.leave()
342	      }
343	
344	      drain.enter()
345	      errPipe.fileHandleForReading.readabilityHandler = { handle in
346	        let data = handle.availableData
347	        if data.isEmpty {
348	          handle.readabilityHandler = nil  // EOF: pipe closed
349	          drain.leave()
350	          return
351	        }
352	        collector.consume(data)
353	      }
354	
355	      let timeoutItem = DispatchWorkItem {
356	        guard !state.isFinished, proc.isRunning else { return }
357	        state.markTimedOut()
358	        proc.terminate()
359	        // NOTE: full process-group kill (also reaping git/jj grandchildren)
360	        // would require launching via posix_spawn with setpgid; terminate() +
361	        // GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 is sufficient for the MVP.
362	        DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 2) {
363	          if proc.isRunning { kill(proc.processIdentifier, SIGKILL) }
364	        }
365	      }
366	      DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + timeout, execute: timeoutItem)
367	
368	      proc.terminationHandler = { finishedProc in
369	        state.markFinished()
370	        timeoutItem.cancel()
371	        drain.wait()
372	        continuation.resume(
373	          returning: CLIResult(
374	            stdout: state.stdout,
375	            stderr: collector.rawString,
376	            exitCode: finishedProc.terminationStatus,
377	            timedOut: state.timedOut,
378	            signaled: finishedProc.terminationReason == .uncaughtSignal
379	          ))
380	      }
381	
382	      do {
383	        try proc.run()
384	      } catch {
385	        errPipe.fileHandleForReading.readabilityHandler = nil
386	        continuation.resume(throwing: error)
387	      }
388	    }
389	  }
390	}

### `SessionByteQueue`'s `wouldBlock` path has no dedicated test (macapp) — FIXED, 2026-08-16

Moved `SessionByteQueue` + `SessionIO` + the two outcome enums from `WorkroomSession/SessionSupport.swift`
into `WorkroomSessionProtocol/SessionIO.swift` (marked `public`) — the module already shared by
`WorkroomApp`, `WorkroomAppTests`, and `workroom-session`, per the second option this entry named.
`WorkroomAppTests/Session/SessionByteQueueTests.swift` now drives `drain`'s `wouldBlock` path against
a real, unread, non-blocking pipe (not a mock): a short write that would block, the queue left
correctly positioned, then a full flush once the reader catches up.

**Trap while writing the test:** the first version set only the pipe's WRITE end non-blocking. The
read-back loop's `SessionIO.read(readFD)` then blocked for real once the currently-buffered bytes
were drained — hanging the test host (`Workroom Dev.app`, beach-balling) rather than failing, since
the block happens deep inside a real `read()` syscall on the main test thread. Both ends of a pipe

### `AppStore`'s default `cli` isn't hardened against a forgotten test double (macapp) — filed 2026-08-16

**What:** `AppStore.init(cli: WorkroomCLIProtocol? = nil, ...)` defaults an un-injected `cli` to the
real `WorkroomCLI.shared` — including under XCTest. A test that constructs a bare `AppStore()`,
leaves `projectStore.projects` empty, and calls `bootstrap()`/`reload()` would silently shell out to
the real bundled `workroom` binary and read the developer's actual `~/.config/workroom/config.json`.

**Why not fixed now:** traced every current call site (`AppStoreSessionRestoreTests`'s two
`bootstrap()` calls) — both pre-seed `projectStore.projects`, so `bootstrap` takes the
`apply(projectStore.projects)` branch and never reaches `cli.list`. Nothing is broken today; this is
defense against a future test, not a current bug. See the 2026-08-16 "Recently done" entry above for
the actual bug this session found and fixed (the shared window's own bootstrap, not this).

**How to start:** default the un-injected `cli` to a `WorkroomCLIProtocol` conformer, active only
under `XCTestConfigurationFilePath != nil`, whose every method throws immediately — a test that
forgot to inject a fake gets a loud, specific failure instead of a silent real-data read.

**Depends on:** nothing blocking.

**Priority:** P3 — hardening, not a known bug.

56	# would race — override with `make app-test APP_TEST_FLAGS=` to bisect a suspected parallel-only

1900	syntax itself works (`Config.zig:9837` `Theme.parseCLI` — `light:`/`dark:` keys, both required,
1901	order-independent). But "the engine picks the variant itself" is false for a *live* surface:
1902	
1903	- Which variant applies is resolved once, at config-derive time, from `_conditional_state.theme`
1904	  (`Config.zig:4457`).
1905	- `ghostty_app_set_color_scheme`/`ghostty_surface_set_color_scheme` (App.zig `colorSchemeEvent`,
1906	  Surface.zig:4716 `colorSchemeCallback`) only **flip that state and fire a
1907	  `.reload_config{.soft=true}` action** — neither one re-derives the config itself.
1908	- `apprt/embedded.zig:267` `performAction` forwards every action straight to the host `action_cb`;
1909	  there is no internal embedded-apprt handler that re-derives on our behalf.
1910	- `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift:127` doesn't handle `GHOSTTY_ACTION_RELOAD_CONFIG` — it falls into
1911	  `default:` → `logUnhandled` → returns `false`.
1912	
1913	So adopting this syntax needs either (a) implementing that action for both the app-scoped and
1914	surface-scoped case, which means calling `ghostty_app_update_config`/`ghostty_surface_update_config`
1915	back into the engine from inside `action_cb` while it's mid-`colorSchemeEvent` — the same kind of
1916	reentrancy-off-callback-stacks hazard flagged for surface teardown (see the libghostty-surface-free
1917	memory note) — or (b) keeping our own explicit `updateConfig` calls, where scheme-flip-before-derive
1918	becomes a newly load-bearing ordering invariant (today's `applyThemeToAll` calls `reloadConfig`
1919	*before* `setColorScheme`, which is harmless only because today's single-name theme has no
1920	conditional state to get stale).
1921	
1922	**Verdict:** not a fit for a pre-release stability batch. There's no bug behind the current
1923	single-name-per-appearance path — it's shipped and correct — and the two ways to land the native
1924	syntax are either an engine-callback reentrancy change or a same-risk reorder of existing calls, both
1925	only verifiable by manually flip-testing OS appearance against live terminals. Re-pricing from "emit
1926	both names once, drop `force:`" to "action-handling change with a re-entrancy hazard and a new
1927	ordering invariant."
1928	
1929	**Priority:** P2 → hold. Re-open only alongside deliberate engine-callback work, not as a drive-by.

1	import CoreGraphics
2	
3	// Pure geometry for the two horizontal tab strips — the terminal strip (`TerminalTabStrip`) and the
4	// Workrooms tab bar (`WorkroomTabBar`). Everything here is view-free so it's unit-testable, and
5	// shared so the two strips can't drift: drag-to-reorder (`TabReorder`, issue #23), the
6	// overflow/pinning decision and its constants (`TabStripOverflow` / `TabStripMetrics`, issue #129),
7	// and the split-group bracket's geometry (`TabStripSplitRun`).
8	
9	/// Pure drag-to-reorder math, shared by the terminal tab strip (`TerminalTabStrip`) and the
10	/// Workrooms tab bar (`WorkroomTabBar`, issue #23). Lifted out of `TerminalTabStrip` so the index
11	/// resolution and gap offsets are unit-testable without a view, and the two strips can't drift.
12	///
13	/// Operates on **position-indexed** chip widths (`widths[i]` is the natural width of the chip at
14	/// position `i`), so it's agnostic to what the chips are — terminal tabs (`UUID`) or workroom
15	/// targets (`String`). The caller maps its own model to a `[CGFloat]` before calling.
16	enum TabReorder {
17	  /// Where the dragged chip lands given its current translation: walk outward from `draggedIndex`,
18	  /// crossing each neighbour once the drag passes that neighbour's half-width (chip width +
19	  /// `spacing`). Reaches index 0 and the last slot.
20	  static func dropTargetIndex(
21	    widths: [CGFloat], draggedIndex di: Int, translation: CGFloat, spacing: CGFloat
22	  ) -> Int {
23	    var idx = di
24	    if translation > 0 {
25	      var accumulated: CGFloat = 0
26	      var j = di + 1
27	      while j < widths.count {
28	        let span = widths[j] + spacing
29	        if translation > accumulated + span / 2 {
30	          idx = j
31	          accumulated += span
32	          j += 1
33	        } else {
34	          break
35	        }
36	      }
37	    } else if translation < 0 {
38	      var accumulated: CGFloat = 0
39	      var j = di - 1
40	      while j >= 0 {
41	        let span = widths[j] + spacing
42	        if -translation > accumulated + span / 2 {
43	          idx = j
44	          accumulated += span
45	          j -= 1
46	        } else {
47	          break
48	        }
49	      }
50	    }
51	    return idx
52	  }
53	
54	  /// Horizontal shift for a non-dragged chip at `index` so the row opens a gap at the drop `target`.
55	  /// `amount` is the dragged chip's width plus inter-chip spacing.
56	  static func gapShift(index: Int, draggedIndex: Int?, target: Int?, amount: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
57	    guard let di = draggedIndex, let ti = target else { return 0 }
58	    if di < ti, index > di, index <= ti { return -amount }  // dragging right: slide left
59	    if di > ti, index >= ti, index < di { return amount }  // dragging left: slide right
60	    return 0
61	  }
62	}
63	
64	/// Shared drag-to-reorder STATE for a horizontal tab strip (issue #23), generic over the chip
65	/// identity type (`TerminalTab.ID` for `TerminalTabStrip`, `SidebarID` for `WorkroomTabBar`) — the
66	/// stateful choreography around `TabReorder`'s pure math, which had drifted into two
67	/// hand-synchronized copies. Both strips independently discovered and fixed the SAME bug: `commit`
68	/// must resolve off the gesture's own final translation, never the live `translation` this type
69	/// tracks for rendering, because a fast/coarse drag's last `onChanged` sample can land short of
70	/// `onEnded`'s true displacement. Each strip owns one `@State private var drag = TabReorderDrag<ID>()`
71	/// and supplies its own commit action and drop-into-pane wiring as call-site closures — the
72	/// division of labor `TabReorder` already uses successfully. Reorder-clamping (`WorkroomTabBar`'s
73	/// `clampReorder`, absent in `TerminalTabStrip`) stays a call-site transform on `finalTranslation`/
74	/// `translation`, not a flag on this type.
75	struct TabReorderDrag<ID: Hashable> {
76	  /// The chip currently dragging, or nil.
77	  private(set) var id: ID?
78	  /// Live translation for the render-time gap preview — NOT what `commit` resolves against.
79	  private(set) var translation: CGFloat = 0
80	  private(set) var widths: [ID: CGFloat] = [:]
81	
82	  var isDragging: Bool { id != nil }
83	
84	  /// The dragged chip's own measured width, or 0 while nothing is dragging / unmeasured.
85	  var draggedWidth: CGFloat { id.flatMap { widths[$0] } ?? 0 }
86	
87	  mutating func setWidths(_ widths: [ID: CGFloat]) { self.widths = widths }
88	
89	  /// `DragGesture.onChanged` handler: latches `id` on the first call for this drag (subsequent
90	  /// calls for a different id are ignored — mirrors both strips' `if draggingID == nil` guard),
91	  /// then records the live translation for the render pass.
92	  mutating func update(_ chipID: ID, translation: CGFloat) {
93	    if id == nil { id = chipID }
94	    guard id == chipID else { return }
95	    self.translation = translation
96	  }
97	
98	  /// Where the dragged chip would land right now, for the render-time gap preview. `nil` while
99	  /// nothing is dragging, the dragged id isn't present in `ids`, or `suspendedByPaneDrag` is true
100	  /// (a chip dragged down into a pane stops opening a reorder gap).
101	  func dropIndex(ids: [ID], spacing: CGFloat, suspendedByPaneDrag: Bool) -> Int? {
102	    guard !suspendedByPaneDrag, let id, let di = ids.firstIndex(of: id) else { return nil }
103	    return TabReorder.dropTargetIndex(
104	      widths: ids.map { widths[$0] ?? 0 }, draggedIndex: di, translation: translation,
105	      spacing: spacing)
106	  }
107	
108	  /// Resolve + clear the drag on drop. `finalTranslation` must be the gesture's own final value
109	  /// (`onEnded`'s `value.translation`), never `translation` above — see the type's doc. Returns
110	  /// the reorder to perform (`from`/`to` position indices), or `nil` when nothing was dragging or
111	  /// the drop index didn't move (a caller that always wants to call its move action anyway can
112	  /// ignore the nil case and use `id`/`ids.firstIndex(of:)` itself, but neither strip needs that).
113	  mutating func commit(ids: [ID], spacing: CGFloat, finalTranslation: CGFloat) -> (
114	    from: Int, to: Int
115	  )? {
116	    defer {
117	      id = nil
118	      translation = 0
119	    }
120	    guard let id, let di = ids.firstIndex(of: id) else { return nil }
121	    let ti = TabReorder.dropTargetIndex(
122	      widths: ids.map { widths[$0] ?? 0 }, draggedIndex: di, translation: finalTranslation,
123	      spacing: spacing)
124	    return ti != di ? (di, ti) : nil
125	  }
126	
127	  /// Clear the drag without resolving a reorder (e.g. dropped into a pane instead).
128	  mutating func cancel() {
129	    id = nil
130	    translation = 0
131	  }
132	}
133	
134	/// Geometry both tab strips must agree on (issue #129). One home, because the title-bar Workrooms bar
135	/// and the terminal strip are on screen at the same time — a fade or gutter that differs between them
136	/// is directly comparable, so a per-view copy of these numbers would drift visibly.
137	enum TabStripMetrics {
138	  /// Gap between the scrolling chip run and the pinned trailing controls, so a clipped chip never
139	  /// abuts them. Passed as the `spacing:` of the controls' `safeAreaInset`, which also *reserves* the
140	  /// controls' own width — so this is the only hand-set number in that relationship.
141	  static let gutter: CGFloat = 8
142	  /// Width of the dissolve at the scroller's trailing edge, so a clipped chip fades out instead of
143	  /// being cut mid-glyph. Deliberately equal to the scroll content's trailing inset: at full
144	  /// scroll-end the ramp then lands on empty margin and the last chip renders crisp, so the fade only
145	  /// ever dissolves content that really is cut off.
146	  static let fade: CGFloat = 8
147	  /// The *inline* "+"'s own leading pad (it hugs the last chip). Applied by the call site, not by the
148	  /// button, so the button's measured width stays free of positioning padding.
149	  static let inlineAddLead: CGFloat = 2
150	  /// Sub-pixel slack in the overflow comparison, so a live window resize can't thrash the mode on
151	  /// rounding alone.
152	  static let epsilon: CGFloat = 0.5
153	  /// Widest a chip's title renders before it tail-truncates (the ellipsis + tooltip carry the rest).
154	  /// One number for both strips *and* the workroom pane header, which deliberately matches them: all
155	  /// three can be on screen at once, so a per-view copy — this was three, each cross-referenced only by
156	  /// comment — is directly comparable and drifts visibly. Note a workroom chip spends it on two names
157	  /// (project + workroom) against a terminal chip's one, so it starts truncating sooner.
158	  static let maxChipTitle: CGFloat = 180
159	}
160	
161	/// The overflow decision for a horizontal tab strip (issue #129): does the *inline* layout — the chip
162	/// run with the "+" hugging the last chip — still fit the width available to it? When it doesn't, the
163	/// trailing controls lift out of the scroller and pin at its trailing edge, so the "+" is always
164	/// reachable.
165	enum TabStripOverflow {
166	  /// Natural width of a chip run: every chip plus the inter-chip spacing.
167	  static func runWidth(_ widths: [CGFloat], spacing: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
168	    guard !widths.isEmpty else { return 0 }
169	    return widths.reduce(0, +) + spacing * CGFloat(widths.count - 1)
170	  }
171	
172	  /// Whether the trailing controls must pin.
173	  ///
174	  /// Takes **only** quantities that are independent of where those controls currently sit, so the
175	  /// answer cannot depend on the layout it selects: the predicate has one fixed point and cannot
176	  /// oscillate as the window resizes. There is deliberately no `isPinned` parameter — a
177	  /// "scroll content vs viewport" comparison *would* oscillate, because lifting the controls out
178	  /// shrinks the content and the viewport by different amounts, leaving a band of widths that pins,
179	  /// then fits, then pins.
180	  ///
181	  /// - Parameters:
182	  ///   - runWidth: measured width of the whole chip run **including the trailing divider and its
183	  ///     pads** — the divider lives inside the measured run and is toggled by opacity, never removed,
184	  ///     so it is always laid out. Passing a chips-only width would let the boundary tests pass while
185	  ///     the rendered threshold sits a few points off.
186	  ///   - add: the trailing controls' intrinsic width, without any positioning pad.
187	  ///   - available: width the strip has for the chips + controls (its own width minus any
188	  ///     fixed-size sibling such as the per-tab toolbar).
189	  ///   - leadingInset: the row's leading inset (4pt in a workroom split, else 8pt).
190	  ///   - inlineAddLead: gap between the run and the controls while inline (spacing + their own pad).
191	  static func pinsControls(
192	    runWidth: CGFloat, add: CGFloat, available: CGFloat,
193	    leadingInset: CGFloat, inlineAddLead: CGFloat, gutter: CGFloat = TabStripMetrics.gutter,
194	    epsilon: CGFloat = TabStripMetrics.epsilon
195	  ) -> Bool {
196	    // Nothing measured yet (first layout pass): render inline. Every input is branch-independent, so
197	    // the correction that follows happens exactly once — it can't become a loop.
198	    guard available > 0, runWidth > 0, add > 0 else { return false }
199	    let inlineWidth = leadingInset + runWidth + inlineAddLead + add + gutter
200	    return inlineWidth > available + epsilon
201	  }
202	}
203	
204	/// Geometry of a split group's contiguous chip run within a strip — the `x`/`width` of the rounded
205	/// bracket drawn around the members (issue #3). Lifted out of `TerminalTabStrip.splitRunRect` so the
206	/// arithmetic is unit-testable without a view, and so it shares one summation with
207	/// `TabStripOverflow.runWidth` instead of carrying a second copy of it.
208	enum TabStripSplitRun {
209	  /// - Parameters:
210	  ///   - widths: position-indexed chip widths (`widths[i]` is the chip at position `i`).
211	  ///   - memberIndices: positions of the group's members. Guaranteed contiguous by the caller's
212	  ///     display order; only the first and last are used, so a stray gap is spanned rather than
213	  ///     rejected.
214	  ///   - spacing: the strip's inter-chip spacing.
215	  /// - Returns: `nil` when there's no real split (fewer than two members) or the indices are out of
216	  ///   range — both mean "draw no bracket".
217	  static func rect(widths: [CGFloat], memberIndices: [Int], spacing: CGFloat)
218	    -> (x: CGFloat, width: CGFloat)?
219	  {
220	    guard memberIndices.count >= 2,
221	      let first = memberIndices.min(), let last = memberIndices.max(),
222	      first >= 0, last < widths.count
223	    else { return nil }
224	    // x: everything before the first member, chips + the spacing that follows each of them.
225	    var x: CGFloat = 0
226	    for i in 0..<first { x += widths[i] + spacing }
227	    // width: the members' own chips, plus the spacing *between* them (one fewer gap than chips).
228	    var width: CGFloat = 0
229	    for i in first...last { width += widths[i] }
230	    width += spacing * CGFloat(last - first)
231	    return (x, width)
232	  }
233	}

landed correctly; what the manual flick surfaced was a visual glitch on the SUCCESS path: the dragged
chip visibly flicked back to its pre-drag position for one frame, THEN the reorder animated it to its
new home — reads as "the drag failed, then something else moved it." Root cause: both strips'
commit function called `drag.commit(...)` (which resets `drag.id`/`translation` — the state driving

unanimated, one render pass before the reorder's own animated transition started. Fixed by moving the

`WorkroomTabBar.commitDrag`, so the offset resetting to 0 and the array reordering land in the same
animated transaction — one continuous motion from under the cursor to the new slot, whether or not a
reorder actually resulted.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/.claude/skills/curate-release

Tag-driven (see README "Releases"). After a release publishes, **curate its GitHub release
notes** — replace GoReleaser's raw commit list with a succinct, themed summary in the style of
`v2.0.0-beta.1` (a headline, a one-line framing, and grouped bullets). The commit list is what
the git log is for.

**Never hard-wrap paragraph or bullet text at a fixed column.** Write each paragraph and each
bullet as one unbroken line, however long. The in-app "What's New" viewer renders a literal `\n`
as a line break instead of reflowing it, so a source line wrapped at ~90 cols shows up as a
sentence broken mid-clause. Markdown block structure (headers, blank lines between paragraphs,
`-` bullets, blockquotes) is unaffected — only the wrapping *within* a block must go.

**Release channels** (issue #91) ship as **two products**. The **main** product (`workroom` CLI +
"Workroom" app) tracks `stable` or `pre`, chosen at runtime (`workroom update --channel stable|pre`;
the app's Settings picker). **Nightly** is a **separate side-by-side install** — a `workroom-nightly`
binary (baked `-X main.channel=nightly`) and a distinct "Workroom Nightly" app (`Nightly` build
config in `project.yml`: bundle id `…workroom.nightly`, `AppIcon-Nightly`, `WorkroomReleaseChannel`
Info.plist marker). Channel is a runtime pref for stable/pre, a build identity for nightly, so
nothing can drift/collide (the main binary rejects `--channel nightly`).

Canonical tag→channel classification is `internal/channel` (Go), mirrored by
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ReleaseChannel.swift` and `macapp/Scripts/channel-helper.sh` — **keep the
three in lockstep**. The updater selects per channel (stable = `/releases/latest` for byte-parity;
pre = `/releases` list, newest stable-or-prerelease; nightly = the fixed `nightly` release by tag),
orders nightlies by the monotonic commit-count and everything else by semver, and verifies against
`checksums.txt`. Nightly is a scheduled build (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`, daily cron;
`CONFIGURATION=Nightly make app-release`) on a fixed `nightly` prerelease; all appcast-writing
workflows share a `concurrency: appcast-feed` group.

```bash
make app-release   # Release build → notarize → staple → drag-to-Applications DMG (Scripts/release.sh)
```

CI authenticates notarytool with an App Store Connect API key instead of the keychain
profile — set `NOTARY_KEY_PATH` (a `.p8`), `NOTARY_KEY_ID`, and `NOTARY_ISSUER_ID` and the
script uses those automatically.

libghostty-spm package, add the `WorkroomApp/` sources, and add `Scripts/build-helper.sh`

## Auto-update (Sparkle)

The app self-updates via [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org): it polls an *appcast* feed and
installs newer, EdDSA-signed DMGs. Wiring lives in `Core/Updater.swift` (the "Check for
Updates…" menu item and the Settings toggle); the `SU*` keys in `project.yml` set the feed URL,
the public key, and automatic checks (on by default). The update artifact is the same notarized
DMG we ship, signed with an Ed25519 key whose **public** half is embedded as `SUPublicEDKey`.

(`…/releases/download/appcast/appcast.xml`); each `v*` release appends an item to it via
`Scripts/appcast.sh`. Versioning is tag-driven: `release.sh` sets `CFBundleShortVersionString`
from the tag and `CFBundleVersion` to the commit count (monotonic, so Sparkle always sees a newer
release as an upgrade).

refreshes the in-app changelog automatically. Fix a published feed by hand with
`TAG=vX.Y.Z REPO=owner/repo GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`.

input.content:
## Persistent terminal sessions

The headline of this beta: ordinary terminals now survive quitting the app. A new background session daemon keeps your shells running independently of the app process, so reattaching after a relaunch picks up exactly where you left off — scrollback and all — replacing the old scrollback-sidecar approach entirely.

> ⚠️ This is a beta — expect rough edges.

### macOS app
- Ordinary terminals persist across quit and relaunch; reattach forces a genuine redraw so a TUI never comes back blank, and titles/cwd/agent-footer usage survive the restart too
- Agent usage: quota and pace now show live in the terminal footer, with a detail popover on tap ("Background sessions" renamed to "Persist sessions" in Settings, with an explanation of what it does)
- libghostty engine bumped 1.2.3 → 1.3.2 (332b2aef → 35e1a016) — fixes a real memory leak in accessibility reads, confirmed with before/after leak counts
- Menu bar icon now matches the square-blocks logo
- Status-aware avatar image loader replaces `AsyncImage`, fixing a stale in-flight-fetch overwrite and an LRU eviction bug
- Tab reorder drag: fixed committing off a stale mid-drag position instead of the gesture's true release point, and a visible flick-back before the reorder animated in
- Working-copy diffs now combine staged and unstaged edits into one view instead of only showing one side
- A stopped run pane now warns instead of silently closing when its command is cleared; a dead supervisor respawn correctly reports stopped instead of looking still-running
- The files panel and diff viewer no longer rebuild/recompute on every unrelated store update

### CLI
- `list`/`list --json` warning logic unified, fixing a real divergence between the two
- `update` now sets the right command context for its JSON error envelope
